name: Plumbing
meta: DIY plumbing repair guides: fix a running toilet, leaky faucet, clogged drain, leaking P-trap, low water pressure and a water heater with no hot water.
intro: Most plumbing problems in a house come down to a worn rubber part, a clog, or a loose connection. These guides walk through the fixes that need only hand tools and a shutoff valve.
safety: Know where your main water shutoff is before you start any plumbing job. Gas water heater problems beyond checking the pilot belong to a licensed plumber or gas technician.
diy_line: Replacing flappers, fill valves, faucet cartridges, aerators and P-traps, and clearing clogs with a plunger or hand auger are all reasonable DIY jobs. Moving pipes, adding fixtures, sewer line problems, and gas connections usually need a licensed plumber and often a permit.

name: Electrical
meta: DIY electrical guides with safety warnings: reset a tripped GFCI or breaker, replace a light switch or outlet, and stop a chirping smoke alarm.
intro: A few electrical jobs are within reach for a careful homeowner, as long as the power is off and verified off. These guides say clearly where the DIY line is and when an electrician is required.
safety: Turn off the breaker and test that the power is off before touching any wire. Local codes and permit rules vary; many places require a licensed electrician for new circuits and panel work. When in doubt, call one.
diy_line: Resetting breakers and GFCIs, testing and replacing smoke alarms, and swapping a like-for-like switch or outlet on an existing circuit are common homeowner jobs where codes allow. New circuits, panel work, aluminum wiring, and anything that keeps tripping are jobs for a licensed electrician.

name: Walls and Tile
meta: DIY wall repair guides: patch small and large drywall holes, fix nail pops, recaulk a bathtub and regrout tile, step by step.
intro: Drywall dents, holes, nail pops and tired bathroom caulk are the most common cosmetic repairs in a house. All of them are learnable with a putty knife, patience and thin coats.
safety: Homes built before 1978 may have lead paint. Do not dry-sand or scrape old painted surfaces until you know; follow EPA lead-safe practices or test first.
diy_line: Patching holes, fixing nail pops, recaulking and regrouting are classic DIY jobs. Large cracks that keep coming back, sagging ceilings, or water stains that spread point to structural or leak problems that need a pro.

name: Doors and Windows
meta: DIY door and window repairs: fix a squeaky door, a door that sticks or will not latch, add weatherstripping, and replace a window screen.
intro: Doors and windows take daily abuse. Squeaks, sticking, latches that miss and drafts usually come from loose hinge screws, seasonal swelling or worn seals, and all have simple fixes.
diy_line: Tightening hinges, lubricating, adjusting strike plates, planing a sticking edge, weatherstripping and rescreening are all DIY friendly. A door or window that suddenly binds along with new wall cracks can point to settling; have it inspected.

name: Appliances
meta: DIY appliance fixes: clear a jammed garbage disposal, a dishwasher that will not drain, a fridge that is not cooling, and a clogged dryer vent.
intro: Before you book a repair visit, a few owner-level checks solve a lot of appliance problems. These guides follow the manufacturers' own troubleshooting steps.
safety: Unplug the appliance or turn off its breaker before reaching inside. Never put your hand into a garbage disposal. Sealed refrigerant, gas and internal electrical repairs are for a qualified technician.
diy_line: Clearing jams, cleaning filters, coils and vents, and checking hoses are owner-level maintenance in most manuals. Replacing motors, control boards, compressors or gas parts is technician work.

name: Outdoor
meta: DIY outdoor home repairs: clean gutters safely, fix a leaky outdoor faucet, and winterize hose bibs before a freeze.
intro: Outdoor maintenance keeps water out of the house. Clean gutters, tight spigots and drained hose bibs prevent the expensive repairs that start with a leak or a frozen pipe.
safety: Ladder work causes many serious home injuries. Use a sound ladder on level ground, keep three points of contact, and look for power lines before you raise it.
diy_line: Gutter cleaning from a ladder, spigot repairs and winterizing are common homeowner jobs. Roof work, two-story gutters, and burst pipes inside walls are good times to call a pro.
